question: Who introduced the Vernacular Press Act in India?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Lord Lytton.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vernacular Press Act

 
 
• 
 The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878 by Lord Lytton.
 
 
• According to this law, the editor of a vernacular newspaper had to get the content reviewed by the police before publishing.
 
• The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in an effort to silence those who were critical of the government.
 
• The Act allowed the government to confiscate the assets of newspapers including their printing presses.
 
• If the newspapers published anything that was found “objectionable”. 
 
• 
 
The act excluded English-language publications.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lord Ripon(1880-1884)

 
 
• ​Lord Ripon is often called the "Father of Local Self-Government" in India.
 
• He introduced the Ilbert Bill in 1883, which aimed to allow Indian judges to try British offenders. 
 
• Ripon expanded access to education through the Hunter Commission, which focused on improving primary and secondary education in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856)**
 
 
• **​**Lord Dalhousie is known for enforcing the Doctrine of Lapse, which allowed the British to annex Indian states if a ruler died without a male heir.
 
• Dalhousie is credited with establishing India's first railway lines and telegraph system, which significantly improved communication and transport.
 
• He introduced a uniform postage system, known as the Indian Postal Service, making mail more accessible and organized throughout the country.
 
 
 
• **Lord Willingdon (1931-1936)**
 
 
• **​**Lord Willingdon was the Viceroy during a critical period of India's freedom struggle
 
 
• particularly during the Civil Disobedience Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
 
 
• During his tenure, the Government of India Act 1935 was passed,
 
 
• which laid the foundation for a federal system in India and increased provincial autonomy.
 
 
 
• He hosted the second and third Round Table Conferences,
 
 
• which aimed to discuss constitutional reforms in India, though they were largely unsuccessful.
